sources.cite: 42 CFR 482.13(e), restraint or seclusion (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-07-16)
sources.note: Relayed from the CMSRN case delirium-night-prn-restraint-order, not re-read for this band; its note: Relayed from the CMSRN course seed, which read the regulation 2026-11-14, not re-read: restraint only when less restrictive measures have failed; never a standing or PRN order; for violent or self-destructive behavior at most 4 hours per adult order, renewed up to 24 hours, with a face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour.

sources.cite: Jaqua EE, Nguyen VTN, Chin E. Delirium in older persons: prevention, evaluation, and management. Am Fam Physician 2023;108(3):278-287
sources.note: Relayed from the CMSRN case delirium-night-prn-restraint-order, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes. Delirium is an 'acute disturbance in attention, cognition, and awareness that fluctuates over time'; precipitants include 'Urinary or stool retention', 'Uncontrolled pain' and 'Infection'; nonpharmacologic measures are 'the foundation of delirium management and prevention'; 'Physical restraints should be avoided because they have been correlated with worse outcomes', used only after other options are exhausted; medication only when conservative treatment fails and agitation is severe.

Relayed from the CMSRN case delirium-night-prn-restraint-order, not re-read for this band; its note: Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model. Disease courses, effect sizes and local waits are authored and carry FLAG.
